intent: Put the A2A inbox bridge and its nats client under the same immutable release and copied-interpreter custody as the autonomous runtime, while preserving a closed command surface and treating bridge heartbeats as delivery observations rather than semantic standing.

commit.message: fix(runtime): lock A2A bridge interpreter custody

interface_mismatches: Four launchd bridge services currently execute through uv --with nats-py, so the Python child comes from a mutable uv build cache rather than the admitted release interpreter.
The immutable release runner currently dispatches only orchestrate-live. Bridge support must be a named closed command that can forward only bridge CLI arguments, never arbitrary modules or scripts.
The repository has no locked A2A runtime extra even though live bridge operation requires nats-py. The release build must sync one exact optional extra into its copied interpreter.
A2A bridge heartbeats and delivery receipts prove bounded transport handling only; they do not prove that a model read, understood, or answered a message.
honest_blockers: Repository tests and a locked dependency prove build-time custody, not a successful launchd cutover or live NATS delivery.
The six-service Mac cutover remains a separately receipted operator action after merge; the unsafe cc85 swarm must not be restarted as rollback.
The optional extra intentionally pins nats-py only. Other A2A tools that require websocket-specific dependencies remain responsible for their own explicit dependency checks.
No bridge heartbeat, durable-consumer state, or model reply is promoted into semantic truth or standing by this packet.
session_entry.rollback: Revert this pull request as one unit and restore bridge launchd plists to the last verified immutable runner configuration. If a live cutover has occurred, roll back bridge and cron services to cc85 only after stopping the new processes; never autonomously restart the quarantined cc85 swarm.
